# Protect Line voice (agent summary)

Distilled from the official tone of voice guide. For the full handbook, see `brand/source/tone-of-voice.md`.

## Purpose

**Investing in Our People to Protect Yours.**

## Name

Always **Protect Line** — two words. Never "Protectline".

## Personality

| We are | We are not |
|--------|------------|
| Friendly | Rude |
| Trustworthy | Dismissive |
| Warm | Sarcastic |
| Professional | Unprofessional |
| Passionate | Arrogant |

## Writing rules

- **British English** — colour, organise, cheque (no American z's)
- **Sentence case** — only capitalise sentences and proper nouns
- **Verbs over nouns** — "start" not "commence", "get" not "obtain"
- **Left-align** long copy; centre only short headlines
- **Explain jargon once**, then use the term
- **Emojis as spice** — not the main course

## Greetings and sign-offs

| Do | Don't |
|----|-------|
| Dear [Name] / Hi [Name] / Hello [Name] | Hey mate / Hiya! / Wassup? |
| All the best / Many thanks / Kind regards | Cheers mate / Peace out! |

## Tone examples

**Good:** "When it comes to whole of life insurance, think of it as a lifelong companion. It's a policy that covers you for your entire life, not just a set period."

**Bad (jargon overload):** "The policyholder, colloquially known as the insured, assumes the financial risk stipulated within an insurance policy."

**Bad (fear-mongering):** "If you neglect life insurance, your family could face insurmountable debts."

**Bad (too vague):** "The insurance buyer takes on financial risk and pays regularly for protection."

## Insurance copy

- Be clear about what cover does without scaring people
- Use standard industry terms (policyholder, premium, beneficiary) with a brief explanation
- Never oversimplify to the point of confusion
- Never use fear tactics or pressure language

## Contact

Questions about brand voice: marketing@protectline.co.uk

# Protect Line — Claude Design bootstrap

For all UI and visual design work, follow the design system in this repository.

## Read order

1. `DESIGN.md` — visual contract (colours, type, components, do/don't)
2. `colors_and_type.css` — CSS custom properties (Claude Design native token file)
3. `components/` — HTML/CSS specimens for each component
4. `kit/index.html` — finished marketing page example
5. `brand/voice.md` — copy tone and voice rules

## Rules

- British English, sentence case, two-word **Protect Line**
- Use **only** colours and spacing from `colors_and_type.css` — never invent hex
- Poppins primary, Lora Bold-Italic accent, Arial email fallback only
- Hot pink sparingly: CTAs, links, Hugo, small accents
- No generic SaaS styling, no fear-mongering tone
- Build desktop **and** mobile variants
- Mark missing assets `[REQUIRES SOURCE]`

## Claude Design setup

1. Link this repo at [claude.ai/design](https://claude.ai/design) → organisation → design system
2. Or run `/design-sync` from Claude Code against this repository
3. Publish the design system so team projects inherit it

## Cursor setup

Open this folder in Cursor. Rules in `.cursor/rules/` load automatically. Ask:

> "Design a [asset type] for Protect Line using the design system."

## Before delivering

- [ ] All colours map to CSS variables
- [ ] Sentence case on headings and body
- [ ] Pink used sparingly
- [ ] Mobile layout checked at 375px
- [ ] Copy matches brand voice (warm, clear, British)

Buttons
